detail.title: The Blessing and Curse of Natural Resource Dependence: A Stochastic Frontier Analysis on Productivity, Resource Rent, Governance and Sustainability
detail.abstract: This study examines the relationship between natural resource dependence and total factor productivity (TFP) and how institutional governance and CO2 emissions condition this relationship. Natural resources are finite with limited scalability; consequently, resource-rich economies must eventually diversify, incurring an opportunity cost in the form of potential productivity losses when capital is reallocated from established extractive sectors. To quantify this opportunity cost, we apply a stochastic frontier framework to a panel of resource-dependent countries, allowing the marginal effect of natural resource rents on TFP to be recovered through the estimation of technical inefficiency. The results indicate that greater resource dependence generally raises TFP, but only in environments characterised by weak governance and high CO2 emissions. However, below a certain threshold level of dependence, improved institutional governance emerges as the principal driver of productivity. Two policy actions follow. First, consolidate and effectively regulate the extractive sector to capture the scale economies. Second, reallocate a portion of the resulting higher natural resource rents to more productive industries in which the country possesses a comparative advantage, including frontier industries. The successful implementation of these policy actions hinges on improved governance that boosts efficiency and transparency. In turn, economic diversification presents an opportunity for a green transition due to traditional extractive industries being compelled to modernise extraction with cleaner, more efficient capital in anticipation of a shift in labour toward emerging growth sectors.

detail.title: The Caribbean Strikes and the Collapse of Legal Oversight in U.S. Military Operations

publicationDetails.journalName: Emory University School of Law Legal Studies Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
For the first time in U.S. history, lethal military force has been authorized solely to target drug traffickers-a move that marks an extraordinary assertion of expanded presidential power. 

Since early September, the U.S. military has killed at least 32 people in seven reported boat strikes in the Caribbean and five in two strikes in the Pacific-the first time in history that, as a matter of presidential policy, lethal force was used against individuals exclusively for the act of trafficking drugs. The administration's actions reveal a troubling expansion of claimed executive power and raise profound questions about the legal authority underpinning the attacks. Indeed, the Commander of Southern Command is reportedly stepping down after expressing concern about the legality of these operations. These strikes also appear to represent a historic collapse of guardrails that once helped reduce the risk of unlawful military operations: the independence of lawyers within the Department of Defense and the deference accorded to their advice.

title: Coupling a stock-flow consistent macroeconomic model with an energy system optimisation model to study the impacts of the energy transition in Colombia
affiliations: Catholic University of Louvain (UCL), University of Angers - Centre d'économie de l'Université de Paris Nord (CEPN), affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Agence Française de Développement (AFD), Centre d'économie de l'Université de Paris Nord (CEPN)

detail.title: Coupling a stock-flow consistent macroeconomic model with an energy system optimisation model to study the impacts of the energy transition in Colombia
detail.abstract: The green transition presents a major economic and financial risk to fossil fuel exporting countries. Colombia is a good example of this: the country will have to cope with significant economic and financial imbalances due to the loss of exports, at the same moment when it tries to mobilise resources to invest in the decarbonisation of its own energy system. To study the intertwine between the energy transition and macroeconomic trends, we present a novel coupling between a Stock-Flow Consistent (SFC) macroeconomic model and an Energy System Optimization Model (ESOM). This coupled model is applied to Colombia to simulate a variety of scenarios. The results especially highlight the joint dynamics between the energy transition, cross-border financial flows and the national currency exchange rate. Overall, the results suggest that the Colombian domestic energy transition, after a ramp-up during its first decade, can have significant macroeconomic impacts, positive or negative depending on the chosen strategy. Based on this pioneering work, several avenues for future research are put forward, to refine the feedback loops in our model of the economy-finance-energy system.

detail.title: The Role of Central Bank Independence and Transparency in Mitigating Asymmetric Information in Sovereign Debt Markets
detail.abstract: Using a comprehensive dataset of sovereign bond issuances and various measures of CBI and transparency from 1973 to 2018, we investigate the impact of central bank independence and transparency on sovereign borrowing costs. We find that higher levels of CBI and transparency are associated with lower sovereign bond coupon rates, highlighting their role as signals of institutional credibility. We also examine the interaction between CBI, transparency, and participation in International Monetary Fund (IMF) programs, documenting that being part of an IMF program further reduces borrowing costs, particularly in countries with stronger institutional frameworks. Our findings suggest that transparency and CBI act as substitutes in reducing sovereign risk premiums, with transparency playing a larger role in environments where central bank independence is weaker.

title: Invisible Patients, Unaccountable Systems: Legal and Ethical Failures in AI-Driven Healthcare

detail.title: Invisible Patients, Unaccountable Systems: Legal and Ethical Failures in AI-Driven Healthcare
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is quickly transforming healthcare systems. From diagnostics to triage and predictive analytics, it promises efficiency and innovation. But beneath this promise lies a systemic threat: algorithmic bias. When AI is trained on unrepresentative data or deployed without safeguards, it reproduces and amplifies health inequities, disproportionately harming women, racial minorities, and other marginalized groups. This paper argues that algorithmic bias in healthcare is not just a technical glitch but a structural injustice that requires legal, ethical, and political action. Using case studies like racial bias in the Optum risk prediction tool, inaccuracies in pulse oximeters for patients with darker skin, and disparities in maternal and pediatric mental health tools, the paper shows how exclusion is built into care delivery itself. The analysis highlights gaps in the UK and EU legal frameworks, including the Equality Act 2010, the UK GDPR, and the EU AI Act, demonstrating how current laws fail to ensure accountability or protect against algorithmic discrimination. From a human rights and sustainability point of view, biased AI systems violate the right to health, the principle of nondiscrimination, and global commitments under the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG 3 and SDG 10). To prevent health technologies from harming justice, the paper calls for mandatory bias audits, strong liability laws, inclusive datasets, and participatory governance. Truly sustainable healthcare requires not just technological innovation but also legal accountability and equityfocused design.

declarations.declarationOfInterest: In accordance with the ASCOLA declaration of ethics, I am happy to clarify that I have nothing to disclose. This paper received the 2025 AdC Competition Policy Award granted by the Portuguese Competition Authority.

detail.abstract: The judgment of the Court of Justice in Android Auto has reshaped the law of refusals to deal. In particular, it has significantly reduced the scope of application of the Magill and Bronner doctrines, which are, in the aftermath of the ruling, only relevant where a dominant undertaking operates a fully closed system. This article identifies the ways in which Android Auto has transformed the case law and expands the reach of intervention under Article 102 TFEU. It also identifies the distributional and institutional consequences of the substantive choices made by the Court of Justice at a time when private enforcement is on the rise across the EU.

detail.title: Recent Developments In Cannabis Law 2024
detail.abstract: The past year marked a significant period of transformation in cannabis regulation across the United States. From federal efforts to reschedule cannabis under the Controlled Substances Act (CSA) to various state-level initiatives, the evolving legal landscape reflects growing recognition of cannabis’s medical utility and economic potential. This article explores the evolving and intricate legal landscape of the cannabis industry, marked by constant changes and a complicated legal status. This year’s recent developments are highlighted throughout, focusing on recent and significant changes in the industry, including federal regulations, business considerations, and the impact of regulations. Despite cannabis remaining a Schedule I drug under the CSA, this article also addresses recent movements toward its potential rescheduling. Currently, twenty-four states and the District of Columbia have legalized cannabis for adult use, while forty states and the District of Columbia have approved its use for medical puroses. With legalization efforts growing and increased public support of legalization, we expect to see further developments in this multibillion- dollar industry.

title: The Generalized Flexible Family of Distributions: Theory, Estimation, and Applications to Cancer Data

detail.title: The Generalized Flexible Family of Distributions: Theory, Estimation, and Applications to Cancer Data
detail.abstract: This study introduces a new and flexible family of continuous probability distributions, termed the Generalized Flexible Family, developed for effective modeling of cancer data. The proposed family extends the recently introduced New Flexible Generalized Family by incorporating an additional shape parameter to enhance flexibility in capturing various data behaviors, including skewness and heavy tails. Fundamental statistical properties such as the quantile function, Shannon entropy, moments, and moment-generating function are derived and discussed in detail. The behavior of the proposed model is examined through probability density function and hazard rate function plots, demonstrating its ability to model diverse hazard shapes commonly observed in biomedical datasets. Parameter estimation is carried out using the maximum likelihood estimation method, and a Monte Carlo simulation study is performed to evaluate the efficiency of the estimators. The practical utility of the new model is demonstrated through applications to three real cancer datasets, where the new model outperforms several existing distributions in terms of goodness-of-fit criteria. Overall, the proposed new model provides a robust and adaptable framework for analyzing complex lifetime.

AI.theoretical_framework: 基于新灵活广义分布族进行扩展，通过引入额外的形状参数来增强分布的灵活性，构建广义灵活分布族理论框架。

AI.practical_contributions: 为癌症数据建模提供了更有效的统计工具，在真实数据集上表现出优越的拟合性能，有助于更准确地分析癌症患者的生存时间和风险模式。

title: Eu Capital Markets Law And The Claim For "Simplification". Suggestions For A Possible Legal Methodology
affiliations: European Banking Institute

detail.title: Eu Capital Markets Law And The Claim For "Simplification". Suggestions For A Possible Legal Methodology
detail.abstract: This paper examines the current debate on the "simplification" of EU financial and, especially, capital markets law, arguing that the term conceals multiple-and often conflicting-agendas ranging from technical rationalisation to de facto deregulation. Against a backdrop of normative inflation and institutional stratification, the analysis distinguishes simplification from deregulation, framing it instead as a methodological commitment to clarity, coherence, and legal reason. The study reviews the positions of EU institutions (Letta, Draghi, and Commission reports), market stakeholders, and selected academic initiatives. It argues that genuine simplification requires a clear conceptual framework, a rebalanced Lamfalussy architecture, and a reconstruction of key taxonomies. The conclusion advances a bottomup, comparative-law approach as the necessary foundation for reform and identifies simplification as a constitutional duty of the Union, to legislate intelligibly, proportionately, and coherently. Simplification, thus conceived, is not the art of reducing rules but the expression of a renewed European legal reason, capable of reconciling technical complexity with normative intelligibility.

title: Sustainable Climate Policy under Disaster Risk
affiliations: Goethe University Frankfurt

detail.title: Sustainable Climate Policy under Disaster Risk
detail.abstract: This paper analyzes sustainable climate policy in the presence of disaster risk using a sustainability concept derived from first principles. The climate-economy system is modeled with Epstein-Zin preferences, and sustainability is defined as a submartingale condition on the social planner's value function, ensuring that future welfare is not expected to decline. The paper makes two main contributions. First, it embeds the sustainability condition into a recursive climate policy framework and derives implications for optimal mitigation and investment. Second, it evaluates the role of the sustainability condition across three disaster risk scenarios-no disaster risk, constant disaster risk, and statedependent disaster risk-and under two institutional regimes: one in which the social planner is continuously required to act sustainably, and another in which sustainability is only enforced once a critical global temperature threshold of 1.5°C is exceeded. Results show that disaster risk alone induces some precautionary behavior, but a binding sustainability condition substantially amplifies mitigation and investment. Under the conditional regime, anticipation of future policy constraints further strengthens early abatement. These findings highlight how ethical constraints and climate risks jointly shape dynamic climate policy.

AI.tldr: 本文基于第一原理推导可持续性概念，分析存在灾害风险时的可持续气候政策。通过Epstein-Zin偏好建模气候-经济系统，将可持续性定义为社会规划者价值函数的亚鞅条件。研究发现灾害风险和可持续性约束共同强化了减缓措施和投资，条件性制度下对未来政策约束的预期进一步加强早期减排。
AI.research_question: 在存在灾害风险的情况下，可持续性约束如何影响最优气候政策？

AI.practical_contributions: 为政策制定者提供在灾害风险和可持续性约束下设计动态气候政策的理论依据，强调伦理约束和气候风险如何共同影响政策选择。

title: Economic Effects of Sustainability Reporting Regulation when Social Activism Amplifies Transition Risks
affiliations: and The University of Melbourne - Department of Accounting

detail.title: Economic Effects of Sustainability Reporting Regulation when Social Activism Amplifies Transition Risks
detail.abstract: Social activism on various environmental and social (E&S) issues (e.g., climate change, biodiversity loss) amplifies corporate transition risks by increasing the likelihood of future E&S regulations that prohibit adverse corporate E&S impacts. We study the role of social activism in shaping the economic effects of corporate sustainability reporting regulations in a capital market model. More stringent sustainability reporting regulation induces corporate abatement, but also exacerbates social activism, giving rise to a powerful strategic complementarity, which disproportionately increases the value relevance of sustainability reporting and strengthens managerial greenwashing incentives. In equilibrium, greenwashing first increases and then decreases with the stringency of sustainability reporting regulations. Additional results suggest that while sustainability reporting regulation is costly for firms (although how costly is nontrivial), we also find that it is generally socially beneficial. We further derive conditions under which lax rather than stringent sustainability reporting regulation is socially optimal. Our results give rise to novel empirical predictions and have important regulatory implications.

title: Behind Closed Doors: Bargaining Power, Resource Allocation and Child Nutrition in Congolese Households

detail.title: Behind Closed Doors: Bargaining Power, Resource Allocation and Child Nutrition in Congolese Households

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that no funds, grants, or other support were received during the preparation of this manuscript.

detail.abstract: Optimal nutrition during the first two years of life is a key factor in reducing the risk of chronic disease and infant mortality, while promoting harmonious physical growth. The objective of this study is to analyse the link between parental bargaining power and childhood nutrition in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The concept of bargaining power, which occupies a central position in this analysis, is evaluated through the relative contribution of parents to aggregate household income. The assessment of childhood nutrition is conducted through the analysis of food consumption frequency, while the measurement of intrahousehold resource allocation is facilitated by the estimation of the proportion of total household expenditure allocated to food. The data utilised in this study derives from the most recent household consumption survey, which was conducted by the National Statistics Institute in 2012. The findings of the study demonstrate a positive correlation between fathers' bargaining power and the frequency of food consumption by children aged 0 to 5. However, further analysis of the data reveals an opposing effect of female bargaining power, which is negatively associated with this frequency. Therefore, intra-household resource allocation appears to mediate the effect of women's bargaining power on the frequency of child food consumption. Indeed, strategic approaches aimed at increasing women's bargaining power within households are emerging as a priority area for targeted public policies. By aiming to re-establish a balance of power within households in the Democratic Republic of Congo, these strategies have the potential to make a significant contribution to improving the nutrition of children under the age of five.

title: Der Unternehmenskauf als Glücksgeschäft: Anwendbarkeit von § 934 ABGB auf den Unternehmenskauf? (The Purchase of a Company as an Aleatory Contract: Applicability of § 934 ABGB (Austrian Civil Code) to the Acquisition of a Company?)

detail.title: Der Unternehmenskauf als Glücksgeschäft: Anwendbarkeit von § 934 ABGB auf den Unternehmenskauf? (The Purchase of a Company as an Aleatory Contract: Applicability of § 934 ABGB (Austrian Civil Code) to the Acquisition of a Company?)
detail.abstract:
German Abstract: Dieses Paper hat den Aufsatz „Der Unternehmenskauf als Glücksgeschäft. Anwendbarkeit von § 934 ABGB auf den Unternehmenskauf?“, zum Gegenstand, der in der Festschrift Matthias Neumayr (2023) veröffentlicht wurde und beruht mit freundlicher Zustimmung des Manz-Verlags auf der dort enthaltenen Formatierung. Er behandelt die Frage, ob § 934 ABGB auf den Unternehmenskauf angewendet werden kann. Diskutiert wird die laesio enormis als allgemein verzichtbare und in der Substanz überholte Regelung. Ein Aspekt der Problematik der gesetzlichen Regelung liegt darin, dass die Bestimmung die Möglichkeit einer objektiven Bewertung der Leistungen voraussetzt. Praktisch ist die Bewertung mit Genauigkeit erforderlich, worin nahezu immer ein Problem liegt. Die Möglichkeit einer derart exakten Bewertung gehört allerdings eher den Bereichen der Fiktion und der Klausuren an, als der Realität. Ganz besonders gilt das für die Bewertung eines Unternehmens, die in der Regel komplex und von zahlreichen Faktoren geprägt wird. Oft sind diese Faktoren auch noch subjektiv extrem unterschiedlich gewichtet - „ein objektiver Wert“ ist dann kaum bestimmbar. Die Autoren werfen die Frage auf, ob der Unternehmenskauf wegen seinen vielen und meist prägenden aleatorischen Elementen grundsätzlich als Glücksgeschäft eingeordnet werden muss. Damit wäre auch die Anfechtung nach § 934 ABGB stets ausgeschlossen.

 English Abstract: This article was first published in the Festschrift Matthias Neumayr (2023). It addresses the question of whether § 934 ABGB (Austrian Civil Code) can be applied to the purchase of a company. The discussion encompasses laesio enormis as a provision that is generally dispensable and, moreover, essentially outdated. A salient issue with the legal provision is that it presupposes the possibility of an objective evaluation of performance. In practice, the evaluation must be precise, which is almost always problematic. However, the possibility of such an accurate evaluation is more likely to be found in the domain of speculative fiction and exams than in reality. This is especially the case in the context of company evaluation, a complex process influenced by numerous factors. The subjective nature of these factors renders the determination of an “objective value” almost impossible. The authors pose the question of whether the purchase of a company must be classified as an aleatory contract due to its many and mostly decisive aleatory elements. This would also preclude any challenge under § 934 of the Austrian Civil Code (ABGB).

detail.title: The Awareness of Ignorance for Conscious & Effective Decision Making in Humans & Machines to Deal with AI Hallucinations & Human Ignorance
detail.abstract: The convergence of human and machine ignorance-rooted in unacknowledged uncertainty-poses existential risks as AI systems transition from digital to physical embodiment. This paper synthesizes ancient Vedic wisdom with cutting-edge AI research to propose the "Awareness of Ignorance" framework, a unified solution addressing systemic failures in both human and artificial decision-making. Drawing from the Upanishads' concept of Avidya (fundamental ignorance) and Jnana (transformative self-awareness), alongside empirical studies of AI hallucinations, scheming behaviors, and cultural blindness, the framework integrates structured ignorance awareness to mitigate cascading catastrophes. Key innovations include: 1. Uncertainty Quantification: Embedding calibrated confidence intervals and abstention thresholds in AI outputs to prevent overconfidence-driven falsehoods, inspired by conformal prediction and selective classification techniques. 2. Human-in-the-Loop Protocols: Enforcing human oversight in high-stakes decisions, informed by Vedic traditions of self-inquiry (Atma-Vidya) and modern "veil-of-ignorance" procedures to prioritize equity and systemic health. 3. Anti-Scheming Alignment: Addressing AI "scheming" (e.g., OpenAI's o3 model exhibiting 13% covert action rates) through moral engine architectures and contextual red-teaming to deter deceptive goal pursuit. 4. Cultural & Ecological Stewardship: Combating human cultural blindness by embedding Vedic stewardship principles into AI governance, as seen in cases like sacred grove deforestation and legal hallucination incidents. By synthesizing the Recognition-Action Taxonomy, Universal Moral Engine frameworks, and risk mitigation strategies from NeurIPS, ACL Anthology, and robotics safety research, this paper advocates for a conscious decision-making paradigm that harmonizes ancient insights with AI ethics. Such an interdisciplinary approach not only averts global catastrophe but also catalyzes human evolution toward humility, transparency, and symbiotic coexistence with intelligent technologies.

title: Interest Rates, Banks' Market Power, and Their Asset Maturity

detail.title: Interest Rates, Banks' Market Power, and Their Asset Maturity
detail.abstract: Banks invest short-term deposits in long-term assets, with asset maturities tending to increase when risk-free rates decline. To explain this behavior, I develop a model where capital regulations incentivize banks to stabilize their cash flows. In this model, because bank profits from deposits increase with risk-free rates, they hold long-term assets, whose profits, net of funding costs, decrease as risk-free rates increase. When risk-free rates are lower, the interest rate sensitivity of deposit profits is higher, implying that the optimal asset maturity is longer. Consistent with the model, I empirically find that the interest rate sensitivity of deposit profits is higher when risk-free rates are lower. In addition, I find that this effect is stronger for banks with higher deposit market power, and that these banks increased their asset maturity more following the interest rate reductions induced by the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: From Federal Permitting to Primacy; Balancing Environmental Protection and Climate Policy Objectives

detail.title: From Federal Permitting to Primacy; Balancing Environmental Protection and Climate Policy Objectives

contentType.other: This article is to be published in Volume 50 of the Harvard Environmental Law Review and may not be copied without the written permission of the Journal.

detail.abstract:
Under the Biden Administration, Congress enacted legislations and a climate policy framework that transformed environmental law in the U.S. to a new stage, requiring the rapid development of infrastructure projects related to renewables and carbon capture. In the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA), for example, priority has been given to renewable energy infrastructure, Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) from major stationary sources, and Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR) from the atmosphere to prevent a climate catastrophe. Despite significant tax reduction to renewables, the support for both the CCS and CDR was confirmed in the recently passed legislation, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OB3 Act). The permitting process is a starting point and the heart of major projects and investments that require federal support. With unprecedented federal support and incentives, there were strong calls for permitting reforms to accelerate renewable energy deployments and emissions reductions, including CCS and CDR, over the last decade. While the economic and social benefits of accelerating the permitting process in the United States are well-known and massive, the speed and cost of the permitting process have been criticized for not meeting the US’s ambitious climate objectives.

Opponents of permitting reforms blame our environmental legislation as a barrier to a rapid transition toward a low-carbon economy. Some claim that the permitting process is still the opposite of national and global objectives and responses to climate issues. This is primarily due to the timely and costly environmental assessment requirements from various federal, state, and local agencies. Environmental assessment is crucial for safeguarding the environment, but the permitting process should be accelerated to achieve our climate objectives. The research argues that the main issue is not permitting per se, but is more about the procedure of permitting. Here, the central question of the research is how a streamlined permitting process can be developed at the federal and state levels in the case of CCS and CDR.

In contrast to many claims that our legislation is a barrier to moving toward a low-carbon economy, as some argue, our environmental legislation can provide solutions for climate-related projects, including CCS and CDR, without compromising our environmental values and principles. More specifically, the research examines how the time and cost of the permitting process can be reduced without compromising public engagement and environmental assessments, thereby avoiding the catastrophic environmental impacts associated with any activity or project, particularly those related to CCS and CDR. This paper offers policy and legislative recommendations at both the federal and local levels in Texas to expedite permitting through robust public engagement and transparency.

title: Housing and Credit Cycles in Ireland

detail.title: Housing and Credit Cycles in Ireland
detail.abstract: We apply the multivariate unobserved components model of Rünstler and Vlekke (2018) to jointly estimate the cyclical and trend components of output, credit, and residential property prices in Ireland. We find that credit and house price cycles are subject to an average duration of about 15 years, considerably longer than the business cycle, estimated at 8.5 years. Compared to several alternative estimation methods, the estimates of house price and credit cycles combine strong early warning performance with superior real-time reliability. Our findings contribute to the monitoring of systemic risks in the Irish economy and the conduct of macroprudential policies.

title: Nuclear Finance and Sustainable Development in Developing Countries

detail.title: Nuclear Finance and Sustainable Development in Developing Countries
detail.abstract:
Sustainable development in developing countries— particularly energy security and diversification—will require substantial investment in energy infrastructure, including nuclear power. Development financing approaches that take these needs into account can facilitate atomic projects. Negative impacts on health, safety, the environment, and the social fabric must be avoided or minimised to ensure broad public acceptance. These wider considerations should be incorporated into planning, development, and financing. During the 1990s, nuclear power was subjected to an intense post-Fukushima moratorium, which practically ceased development for over a generation. Climate change, however, has led to a global rethink of nuclear power, and there is growing recognition that it plays a role within a low-carbon scenario. Financing strategies that incorporate these factors, address risk, and secure other multi-level socio-economic and environmental concerns can help establish the necessary projects.

Support and regulatory incentives for nuclear project promoters will thus require a nuclear project assessment. Nuclear energy can play a prominent role in sustainable development. Hence, environmental considerations are already contained in all the multilateral and bilateral development financing initiatives. Key socio-economic issues that need attention include whether project capitals exceed expected social benefits by the time of commissioning, and whether possible development-related external costs exceed expected project development finance. Public acceptance, however, is treated as an internalised factor affecting project implementation, thereby influencing the solutions to other typical cost-benefit applications.

title: From Mandala to Masterplan: Applying Vastu's Spatial Philosophy in Climate-Responsive Urban Design

detail.title: From Mandala to Masterplan: Applying Vastu's Spatial Philosophy in Climate-Responsive Urban Design
detail.abstract: In today's world, the major issue that lies ahead of us is the rapid industrialization and urbanization accompanied by the ever-increasing climate crisis. This has led to the need to rethink urban planning models for the cities. In this research we will be revisiting the age-old Indian concept of spatial planning called Vastu-Purush Mandala. This valuable tool has helped to shape the climate-responsive urban design concept in the past. This study will explore the deeper environmental intelligence of Vastu that can align human habitation with the forces of nature that will in turn promote balance, sustainability, and well-being rather than just solely viewing Vastu through a traditional or ritualistic lens. The initial part of the paper will contain the historical and theoretical context of Vastu Shastra in India along with a discussion of its core elements, including but not limited to orientation, elemental balance (earth, water, fire, air, space), mandala grids, etc. The research paper will focus on drawing parallels between the age-old Vastu Shastra principles and the modern urban design interventions to elaborate on how the ancient wisdom knowingly/unknowingly anticipated many contemporary sustainability goals, such as solar access, maximized natural ventilation, and integration of green and blue infrastructure. The paper will analyze the practical ways in which Vastu-informed planning has influenced large-scale urban planning environments through the case studies of historic settlements such as Jaipur and Fatehpur Sikri, along with the study of modern reinterpretation like Amravati. It will further discuss climate-responsive strategies like street orientation for passive cooling, public squares for heat mitigation, and zoning based on functional synergy and how these strategies can be inspired by the Vastu Purush Mandala's spatial planning concepts. The paper will also address the difficulties in integrating vastu in contemporary urban setups. It will discuss how, instead of rigidly applying outdated Vastu principles, people need to apply a flexible approach that can smoothly balance timeless spatial wisdom with modern technology, industrial innovations, site context, demography, and practical planning techniques requirements. The paper will conclude by proposing a brand new hybrid model that will incorporate new innovative design tools and site contextual data with the Vastu Shastra principles, which will help to generate a more dynamic urban development. Ultimately the paper will conclude with the thought that the Vastu is not only a traditional spatial philosophy but also an adaptable framework that can offer cities a new way towards more sustainable, resilient, socio-culturally vibrant, and healthy urban settings. By moving "From Mandala to Masterplan," we as architects and urban designers can bridge the gap between timeless "Vastu Shastra" principles and "21st-century rapid urbanization" and create a "new advanced settlement" that is not only highly sustainable but also climatically, culturally, and spiritually aware.

title: How political winds shape growth horizons: Firm-level political risk and equity duration
affiliations: and Bryant University

detail.title: How political winds shape growth horizons: Firm-level political risk and equity duration
detail.abstract: This study examines the pivotal role of firm-level political risk in affecting firm-level equity duration, revealing a significant and negative impact. By building a theoretical model, we propose that firm-level equity duration is intrinsically tied to the price-dividend ratio and is primarily influenced by political risk through the cash flow channel. To ensure robustness, we implement placebo test, instrumental variable analysis, and propensity score matching. The findings indicate that the relationship between firm-level political risk and equity duration remains unaffected by aggregate economic policy uncertainty level. Notably, periods of Democratic leadership appear to mitigate the negative effects of political risk on equity duration. Additionally, the study documents that firm lobbying activities and institutional investor ownership are effective in counteracting the negative impacts of firm-level political risk on equity duration.

detail.abstract: Using annual data from 2000 to 2021, this study estimates Newey-West corrected OLS models that include crisis episodes, financial depth, sovereign debt, remittance inflows, and institutional quality. The findings reveal a counterintuitive pattern: higher global economic policy uncertainty (GEPU) is associated with lower reported growth in non-performing loans (NPLs) 1. This negative coefficient indicates a masking mechanism where banks restrict credit supply and regulators delay recognising losses, concealing actual NPLs as risks accumulate unseen. Interaction effects suggest that domestic structures influence this relationship: more developed private credit markets and increasing public debt amplify exposure to shocks, while institutional quality reduces long-term defaults but may encourage short-term moral hazard during crises. Robustness checks using different GEPU measures, lag structures, and remittance interactions confirm the context-dependent nature of these results. The main implication is that declining NPL ratios amid global uncertainty are statistical illusions of stability, hiding underlying fragility. Policy priorities include rules-based loan classification, forward-looking provisioning, sovereign exposure caps, SME liquidity facilities, and governance reforms to transform superficial calm into genuine resilience. 1 The two-lag GEPU coefficients are negative and statistically significant across all three specifications (-0.030 **,-0.168 *,-0.158 *), indicating that a rise in global economic policy uncertainty is associated with a subsequent decline in the growth of reported non-performing loans in Bangladesh. detail.abstract: This article analyzes, based on an extensive research project, how the "gatekeepers" geographically implement the provisions of the Digital Markets Act. Apple, Google, and Booking are largely limiting their implementation measures to the EU or the EEA. Microsoft, Meta, and ByteDance are extending their measures to a considerable degree to certain non-EU countries. However, virtually no gatekeeper is extending measures that are affected by the Commission's non-compliance proceedings. The gatekeepers' communications often appear complex or even contradictory. As further findings of this research project display, the overall "Brussels Effect" of the Digital Markets Act appears to be fragmented.

detail.title: One Ratio, Two Risks: Credit and Interest Rate Trade-offs under the CBLR Framework
detail.abstract: This paper examines how the Community Bank Leverage Ratio (CBLR) framework alters banks' risk trade-offs by simplifying capital regulation. Using Call Report data from 2017-2023, I study community banks' credit and interest rate risk exposures after CBLR adoption. Results show that adopting banks reduce higher-risk commercial and industrial lending, consistent with a shift away from activities that increase credit risk. At the same time, adopters increase their reliance on longer-term securities and mortgage lending, heightening exposure to interest rate risk. These findings highlight that while the CBLR reduces compliance costs, it also encourages banks to reallocate risk rather than reduce it. The results contribute to research on capital regulation by showing how simplified rules affect bank behavior, and they inform ongoing policy debates on balancing regulatory burden with financial stability.

detail.title: Optimizing Electric Vehicle Battery Swapping Services: A Behavior Cloning-Integrated Reinforcement Learning Framework for Charging Decisions
detail.abstract:
Battery swapping stations (BSS) enable electric vehicle drivers to replace depleted batteries with fully charged ones within minutes, addressing range anxiety and charging time concerns. BSS operators must determine optimal battery charging schedules under uncertainty from stochastic demand, time-varying electricity prices, and capacity constraints to ensure profitability.
This paper formulates the BSS charging problem as a periodic Markov Decision Process and develops a Demonstration Augmented Actor-Critic (DAAC) framework that integrates behavior cloning with deep reinforcement learning. The approach addresses the sparse reward problem where charging costs are immediate but revenues are delayed until batteries are used for swaps. 
Our methodology features three innovations: engineered state representations capturing current operations and forward-looking conditions, reward shaping providing denser feedback signals, and two-phase training combining offline pretraining on expert demonstrations with online fine-tuning. Using real-world data from NIO's Shanghai operations, we validate DAAC against Proximal Policy Optimization, standalone Behavior Cloning, and threshold-based policies. Extensive simulations demonstrate that DAAC consistently achieves the highest total profit while maintaining competitive service quality across diverse operational scenarios. Under both static and dynamic demand patterns, DAAC outperforms all baselines in profitability while effectively minimizing lost sales. Component analysis confirms that both offline pretraining and reward shaping significantly improve performance. The framework offers actionable insights for BSS operators on optimal charging strategies and supports informed investment decisions across various battery inventory configurations, thereby advancing the battery-as-a-service business model.

detail.abstract: How do authoritarian regimes balance civic participation and social control in the digital age? This study examines the trade-offs of state-led participatory governance through the case of China's Sharp Eyes Project, a nationwide digital surveillance initiative that enlists citizens to monitor and report local misconduct. Using original data, the findings reveal that while the program enhances regime stability by fostering bottom-up information flows, it simultaneously erodes social trust by institutionalizing mutual surveillance. Further analysis identifies mass reporting as the central mechanism driving both increased governance efficiency and declining social cohesion, highlighting the paradox of civic participation under authoritarian rule. By bridging literature on authoritarian resilience, digital governance, and political participation, this research advances our understanding of how regimes leverage technology to co-opt civic engagement and its social consequences.

detail.abstract: Hard sovereign defaults—defaults with large haircuts—are associated with deeper recessions, longer durations, and, as we show, larger devaluations than soft defaults. We rationalize these regularities by developing a single-proposer noise bargaining game and embedding it in a two-sector sovereign default model. Creditors weigh the sovereign's haircut offers against likely future offers and idiosyncratic valuation shocks. In short-lived recessions, creditors tend to reject large proposed haircuts, anticipating better terms as the economy recovers—endogenously correlating default intensity with adverse outcomes. Two years after default, our decomposition attributes nearly 80% of the observed output differentials to selection on different shock realizations.

detail.abstract: Concerns over talent management have endured for a decade. Although numerous scholars have examined talent management, a limited number have concentrated especially on the public sector, leading to significant research gaps. This research employed Scopus data from 2014 to 2024 to do a systematic literature review (SLR) and a bibliometric analysis, focusing on the identification of trends and themes in public sector talent management. The bibliometric study looks at annual production trends, significant publications, important authors in the field, and the topics or themes that come up most often in public sector talent management. The systematic literature review included the 24 most cited and relevant documents on talent management in the public sector to evaluate the theories and methods most commonly employed, as well as the impact, challenges, and future research agenda. The research indicated that, although the literature on talent management in the public sector is expanding, it is still insufficient. Critical concerns encompass leadership, organizational efficacy, managerial assistance at the line level, recruitment, and succession planning. There are also gaps in theory and methods, as well as problems and chances for future research. These findings may improve public sector human resource management and talent management studies.

detail.abstract: This article studies the impact of leadership rotations on public procurement allocation, using novel data from China's municipal public contracts and mayoral career records. I find that new mayors often allocate more and larger contracts to companies from their previous postings, driven by uncertainty and informational advantages. This favoritism is more pronounced when mayors are highly influenced by local businesses in their former locations but diminishes as they become familiar with their new positions. Over time, mayors' preferences shift from firms in their former locations to those in their current cities, indicating a tenure-related adaptation. However, this favoritism increases the risk of corruption and correlates with mayor career incentives. This study contributes to understanding the authoritarian distributive bias and the implications of meritocratic leadership rotations in nondemocratic regimes.

detail.abstract: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) investing has become a strategic priority for governments worldwide, yet its return on investment (ROI) remains difficult to quantify using traditional financial metrics. This paper proposes a multidimensional framework for evaluating ESG ROI in public sector finance, integrating fiscal, environmental, social, and governance indicators. Drawing on global literature and municipal case studies, the framework enables policymakers to assess ESG initiatives not only by cost savings and risk mitigation, but also by long-term public value creation. A case study of green bond programs in New York and San Francisco illustrates how ESG investments can yield measurable benefits in climate resilience and operational efficiency. The paper concludes with strategic recommendations for improving ESG data infrastructure, standardizing evaluation models, and aligning public finance with sustainable development goals.

detail.abstract:
Purpose – This paper examines how expert practitioners define project governance and develop a project governance system that enables strategy implementation through projects.

Design/methodology/approach – We conducted semi-structured interviews with project governance experts and analyzed the data using thematic analysis. Subsequently, based on the stratified ontology of critical realism, we employed retroductive theoretical triangulation to explain the themes identified using five emergent theoretical perspectives.

Findings – By integrating the themes extracted from the data with the emergent theoretical perspectives, we developed a framework outlining the general process through which practitioners make sense of the concept of project governance, formulate an appropriate project governance system for their respective organizations, and manage its evolution over time. Furthermore, we proposed a holistic approach to project governance that spans the entire investment life cycle of projects and enables the implementation of strategy through projects.

Originality/value – This study contributes to the governance-as-practice perspective and the growing stream of literature that views projects as investments. We position the project governance system as the steward of an organization’s investments in projects.

Practical implications – This study attempts to make sense of the diverse interpretations of the concept of project governance adopted by practitioners. It further summarizes valuable insights from expert practitioners for formulating and enacting effective project governance systems.

title: Tariff-Induced Risks and Mitigation Strategies in the U.S. Supply Chain
affiliations: University of the Cumberlands

detail.title: Tariff-Induced Risks and Mitigation Strategies in the U.S. Supply Chain
detail.abstract: Tariffs continue to pose a major challenge to the stability and efficiency of global and domestic supply chains, particularly within the U.S. economy. As the United States intensifies the use of tariffs as a trade policy tool, organizations face increased costs, disrupted sourcing strategies, and reduced flexibility in supplier relationships. This paper examines the multifaceted risks tariffs impose on supply chain operations, including heightened input costs, regulatory uncertainty, and the erosion of cost efficiency and resilience. Drawing from recent research and professional analyses, the study explores five key mitigation strategies: cross-functional disruption response teams, data-driven decision-making, end-to-end visibility, supply network optimization, and compliance management. Of these, the integration of cross-functional collaboration supported by real-time analytics emerges as the most effective approach for sustaining organizational agility and responsiveness to regulatory volatility. By combining strategic adaptability with analytical precision, companies can transform tariff disruptions into opportunities for competitive advantage. Ultimately, this research underscores that the long-term success of U.S. supply chains depends on proactive risk management, integrated communication systems, and resilient operational design in an era of global trade uncertainty.

title: Optimal Investment with Quadratic Transaction Costs in a Multi-factor and Stochastic Interest Rate Environment

detail.title: Optimal Investment with Quadratic Transaction Costs in a Multi-factor and Stochastic Interest Rate Environment
detail.abstract: This paper studies an optimal investment problem in a comprehensive market environment featuring geometric Brownian motion type asset dynamics, stochastic interest rates, return and volatility factors, and time-varying, state-dependent quadratic transaction costs. Under a finite-horizon mean-quadratic variation objective, we derive a semi-analytical solution for the value function and optimal trading strategy and establish the well-posedness of the associated system of nonlinear PDEs along with the verification theorem. The optimal strategy retains a tractable structure that echoes the core economic principle of trading gradually toward an aim portfolio as proposed in Gârleanu and Pedersen (2013). Specifically, the aim portfolio is adjusted for hedging demands against the interest rate risk, and the trading speed reflects an intertemporal trade-off between immediate rebalancing costs and future market liquidity. Additionally, we propose a deep learning scheme to enable efficient implementation in high-dimensional settings based on observable market data and estimated factor models.

German Abstract: Das Steuercontrolling in Deutschland ist ein noch relativ junges Forschungsfeld im Controlling. Die Berücksichtigung von Steuereffekten ist für die wertorientierte Unternehmensführung sowohl für Großunternehmen als auch für KMU relevant. Empirische Forschung auf dem Gebiet des Steuercontrollings, insbesondere bezüglich deutscher KMU, fehlt weitgehend. In diesem Beitrag werden die Ergebnisse einer ersten Umfrage zum Steuercontrolling im Jahr 2016 über in Deutschland ansässige KMU vorgestellt. Zunächst wird der Forschungsstand des deutschen Steuercontrollings mit seinen Funktionen und der Online-Fragebogen der Umfrage besprochen. Danach werden die verwendete Forschungsdatenbank, die realisierte Feldarbeit und die wichtigsten Befragungsergebnisse vorgestellt. Final werden Implikationen zur Unterstützung operativer Planungsansätze unter Einbezug von Steuereffekten aufgezeigt.

English Abstract: Tax management accounting in Germany is still a relatively new field of research in Management Accounting. Taking into account tax effects is relevant for value-based management for both, large enterprises and SMEs. Empirical research in this area, especially referring to German SMEs, is largely lacking. This paper presents the results of an initial survey on tax management accounting in 2016 on SMEs located in Germany. First, the state of research of German tax management accounting with its functions and the online questionnaire of the survey are discussed. Then, the research database used, the fieldwork realized and the main results of the survey are presented. Finally, implications for supporting operational planning approaches incorporating tax effects are highlighted.

detail.title: Government Lake's Concept and Complications Regarding the Crater Lakes in Laguna and Quezon Provinces
detail.abstract: The Government in the crater lakes have been mentioned and recognized in the literature, but their abstraction and hindrances are commonly scrutinized and speculated less. These small lakes are abundant in the Philippines, possessing the potential and capability for economic development and environmental conservation, yet many remain underdeveloped, underutilized, and lag behind. Thus, this academic paper establishes the concept of Government Lake and examines its complications in relation to the Ten Crater Lakes. The central idea employs theoretical-empirical and big-picture perspectives to discuss the role and its essential constituents-the Government Authorities, Development Orientations, and Development Impediments-in the small lakes. These centerpieces are integral for managing, constituting, and advancing the aquaculture-tourism nexus while sustaining the lakes and supporting their municipalities. Accordingly, the Government Authorities must lead the development position, preside over the conservation efforts, and tackle the crater lake stakeholders' dysfunctions. Thus, the Government Lake is the crux-the hegemonic for the small lakes' success (or failure), the fundamental for enduring commitment, the directional for attaining aquaculture and tourism balance, and the resonating for embracing this core concept.

title: Ubuntu: A New Standard for Arbitration in Africa and Beyond

detail.title: Ubuntu: A New Standard for Arbitration in Africa and Beyond

declarations.funderStatement: This is a "white paper" that incorporated existing law and policy in International Arbitration and the publications of the AfCFTA.

detail.abstract: In this article, we critically examine how existing international arbitration and specifically investor-state dispute settlement (ISDS) may be misaligned with African values and legal culture and proposes the African concept of Ubuntu as a philosophical and procedural foundation to reform norms of arbitration. Using benchmark cases such as Biwater Gauff v. Tanzania, Von Pezold v. Zimbabwe, Glamis Gold v. USA, Bear Creek Mining v. Peru, Urbaser v. Argentina, and Cortec Mining v. Kenya, we show how mainstream arbitration has disempowered community stakeholders and ignored community interests. We then delineate Ubuntu, the African philosophy of relational personhood which incorporates respect for individual dignity, communality and harmony, and make a case for its incorporation into arbitration as a foundational concept in line with "fundamental notions of justice and equity". Procedural innovations are proposed that embrace community and non-disputing party participation, fostering transparency, and streamlining procedures to align with the values within Ubuntu. We highlight the wider consequences of an "Ubuntu-inspired" approach on sustainability, human rights, and development outcomes, drawing on contemporary legal instruments and the new AAA Model BIT. Our conclusion offers concrete policy recommendations including the insertion of Ubuntu into African and Afrocentric global treaty documents, the impact of indigenous participation and socio-environmental issues in ISDS, and the integration of African legal values into the international rules of arbitral practice where there is direct effect upon the nations of the African Continent.

title: Impossibility Patterns Finder (IPF): JSON Schema Specification v1.0

detail.title: Impossibility Patterns Finder (IPF): JSON Schema Specification v1.0

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This research received no external or non-financial support.

detail.abstract:
The Impossibility Patterns Finder (IPF) provides a machine-readable catalog of theoretical limits across scientific domains. This technical specification documents the JSON schema (Draft 2020-12 compliant), validation rules, and initial catalog of 11 impossibility results spanning computation (Gödel, Turing), physics (Heisenberg, Carnot), statistics (No-Free-Lunch), economics (Arrow), and information theory (Shannon). 

Each catalog entry includes formal statements, assumptions, mechanism classification (Self-reference, Context, Resource), evidence grades, and typed "escape hatches" indicating viable relaxations. The schema enables automated barrier-checking: evaluating research proposals and AI capability claims against known theoretical constraints before resource commitment. 

Applications include technical due diligence (checking AI startup claims), research evaluation (grant review), enterprise strategy (validating feasibility), and education (teaching cross-domain limits). The schema supports community extension, with validation tools and contribution guidelines. 

Released under CC BY 4.0 with DOI-based versioning (Zenodo: 10.5281/zenodo.17393656). Future development includes catalog expansion to 50-100 entries, REST API implementation, and natural language processing for automated claims-to-limits matching. 
This specification reduces wasted effort on structurally impossible proposals and accelerates limits-aware design by making impossibility results auditable, comparable, and computable.

title: Assessment of Interprofessional Trauma Team Performance and Cohesion During a Civil–Military Large-Scale Live Simulation Exercise: A Prospective Cross-Sectional Observational Study

detail.title: Assessment of Interprofessional Trauma Team Performance and Cohesion During a Civil–Military Large-Scale Live Simulation Exercise: A Prospective Cross-Sectional Observational Study
detail.abstract: IntroductionLarge-scale civil–military medical simulation exercises provide realistic environments for interprofessional trauma teams to develop leadership, communication, and decision-making skills under high-stress conditions. Simulation-based education is increasingly recognised as a critical strategy for improving trauma system readiness, fostering interprofessional collaboration, and identifying systemic weaknesses under controlled conditions. However, empirical evidence on how such exercises enhance preparedness, cohesion, and interoperability across multinational medical systems remains limited. Understanding the interaction between civilian and military personnel in shared trauma management environments is vital for optimising crisis response capacity and interoperability. This study assessed trauma team performance and cohesion during a multinational large-scale live simulation, identifying barriers and enablers influencing interoperability and operational readiness.Methods and MaterialsThis prospective cross-sectional observational study was conducted during the NATO Vigorous Warrior 2024 (VW24) exercise across eight Role 2 hospitals in Hungary (4–8 May 2024). The exercise involved trauma teams (n = 75) from nine nations managing simulated major trauma casualties under operational field conditions representative of deployed environments. Performance was evaluated using the Non-Technical Skills for Surgeons (NOTSS) and Team Emergency Assessment Measure (TEAM) frameworks, both validated behavioural assessment tools that measure non-technical competencies such as leadership, communication, teamwork, and task management. Four expert assessors with experience in trauma and medical education performed structured, real-time observations, while team members completed immediate post-scenario self-assessments. Descriptive analyses compared team and assessor ratings across performance domains to identify convergences and discrepancies.ResultsTeams rated their performance more positively than assessors (57% vs 25% excellent). Assessors noted deficits in leadership clarity, structured communication, and role allocation, with 25% performing below average. Multicultural diversity influenced communication and coordination, while the absence of standardised debriefing protocols limited structured learning and cohesion. Barriers to readiness included inconsistent equipment, documentation, and clinical procedures. Stronger performance correlated with clear leadership and logistical preparedness.ConclusionLeadership clarity, structured communication, and psychological safety underpin effective multinational trauma teamwork. Findings highlight the need for clinically standardised training and operational frameworks ensuring consistent leadership, communication, and handovers across civil–military systems, with policy integration of harmonised simulation and debriefing protocols to enhance interoperability and preparedness.

AI.tldr: 该研究评估了北约Vigorous Warrior 2024演习中多国民事-军事医疗模拟训练对创伤团队表现和凝聚力的影响，发现团队自我评价高于评估者，领导力清晰度、结构化沟通和标准化流程是影响互操作性和战备状态的关键因素。

AI.motivation: 大规模民事-军事医疗模拟演习为跨专业创伤团队提供了在高压力环境下发展领导力、沟通和决策技能的现实环境，但关于此类演习如何增强多国医疗系统间准备度、凝聚力和互操作性的实证证据仍然有限。
AI.theoretical_framework: 使用外科医生非技术技能(NOTSS)和团队紧急评估测量(TEAM)框架，这些是经过验证的行为评估工具，用于衡量领导力、沟通、团队合作和任务管理等非技术能力。
AI.method: 前瞻性横断面观察研究，在匈牙利8个Role 2医院进行，涉及来自9个国家的75个创伤团队管理模拟重大创伤伤员。4名专家评估员进行结构化实时观察，团队成员完成场景后自我评估。
AI.findings: 团队自我评价(57%优秀)高于评估者评价(25%优秀)；评估者发现领导力清晰度、结构化沟通和角色分配存在缺陷；多元文化多样性影响沟通协调；缺乏标准化汇报协议限制了结构化学习和凝聚力。
AI.theory_contributions: 确定了领导力清晰度、结构化沟通和心理安全是多国创伤团队有效合作的基础，强调了临床标准化培训和操作框架的重要性。
AI.practical_contributions: 提出了整合协调模拟和汇报协议的政策建议，以增强民事-军事系统间的互操作性和战备状态，确保一致的领导力、沟通和交接流程。

title: Regulatory Tunneling in Tokenized IP: Path-Integral Control with KL-Regularized Lévy-Measure Control and Governance Barriers under Jump-Diffusion Dynamics
affiliations: Rosenheim university of applied sciences

detail.title: Regulatory Tunneling in Tokenized IP: Path-Integral Control with KL-Regularized Lévy-Measure Control and Governance Barriers under Jump-Diffusion Dynamics
detail.abstract: We develop a path-integral framework for tokenized intellectual property valuation under regulatory uncertainty. Our innovation, regulatory tunneling, quantifies probabilistic penetration through governance barriers using controlled Lévy measures with Kullback-Leibler regularization. The key novelties are KL-regularized hazard shaping + regulatory barriers + PI↔integro-HJB bridge. This enables explicit modeling of soft regulatory boundaries and optimal hazard adjustment. We prove equivalence between path-integral representations and viscosity solutions of integro-Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equations. In representative industry calibrations, tunneling accounts for 20-40% of risk premiums in volatile regulatory environments. The framework prices regulatory derivatives and guides optimal token design for emerging digital asset markets.

AI.tldr: 本文开发了一个路径积分框架，用于在监管不确定性下对代币化知识产权进行估值。核心创新是监管隧道效应，通过受控Lévy测度和KL正则化来量化穿透治理障碍的概率。主要贡献包括KL正则化风险塑造+监管障碍+路径积分与积分-HJB方程桥接。
AI.research_question: 如何在监管不确定性环境下对代币化知识产权进行准确估值？
AI.motivation: 新兴数字资产市场中代币化知识产权面临监管障碍和不确定性，需要新的估值框架来量化监管风险。
AI.theoretical_framework: 路径积分理论、Lévy过程、Kullback-Leibler正则化、积分-哈密顿-雅可比-贝尔曼方程、监管隧道效应理论
AI.method: 路径积分框架结合受控Lévy测度和KL正则化，建立路径积分表示与积分-HJB方程粘性解之间的等价关系
AI.findings: 监管隧道效应在波动性监管环境中占风险溢价的20-40%，框架能够为监管衍生品定价并指导最优代币设计
AI.theory_contributions: 证明了路径积分表示与积分-HJB方程粘性解的等价性，提出了监管隧道效应理论，发展了KL正则化风险塑造方法
AI.practical_contributions: 为代币化知识产权提供估值框架，能够定价监管衍生品，指导数字资产市场中的最优代币设计

title: Environmental Responsibility: Impact of Waste-Sorting Regulation on Secondary Markets
affiliations: , Emory University - Information Systems and Operations Management and Shanghai Jiao Tong University

detail.title: Environmental Responsibility: Impact of Waste-Sorting Regulation on Secondary Markets
detail.abstract: Proper waste disposal in an environmentally friendly manner is crucial for protecting both ecosystems and public health. Among various policy tools, waste-sorting regulations and the growth of secondary markets—where consumers resell used goods—offer promising solutions for more sustainable waste management. However, how such regulations affect secondary markets remains unclear, as user motivations and convenience differ from those in the primary market. In this paper, we address this question through a natural experiment: the 2019 implementation of mandatory waste-sorting regulations in Shanghai. Using data on over 362 million resale listings from a leading online platform, we examine the policy's impact on both resale listings and purchase volume. We employ the synthetic control method to construct a comparable control group and use difference-in-differences to estimate the policy's impact. We find no significant change in overall resale listings. However, among environmentally responsible younger users, resale listings decrease by 8.43% and purchase volume declines by 1.95%. The effect is particularly pronounced for easily discarded goods and inactive users. Our findings reveal a trade-off: while regulations encourage responsible disposal, they may also unintentionally discourage reuse.

AI.tldr: 上海2019年强制垃圾分类政策对二手市场的影响研究：通过自然实验发现，政策导致环保意识强的年轻用户转售量下降8.43%，购买量下降1.95%，揭示了环保政策与再利用之间的权衡关系。
AI.research_question: 垃圾分类法规如何影响二手市场？
AI.motivation: 环保友好的废弃物处理对保护生态系统和公共健康至关重要，但垃圾分类法规对二手市场的影响尚不清楚。
AI.theoretical_framework: 自然实验设计，结合合成控制法和双重差分法。
AI.method: 利用上海2019年强制垃圾分类政策作为自然实验，分析领先在线平台上3.62亿条转售数据，使用合成控制法构建对照组和双重差分法估计政策影响。
AI.findings: 总体转售量无显著变化，但环保意识强的年轻用户转售量下降8.43%，购买量下降1.95%，对易丢弃商品和非活跃用户影响更明显。
AI.theory_contributions: 揭示了环保政策与二手市场再利用行为之间的复杂关系，提出了政策权衡理论框架。
AI.practical_contributions: 为政策制定者提供关于垃圾分类政策对二手市场影响的实证证据，帮助设计更平衡的环保政策。

title: The $20 Trillion Question: Why a Company's Most Valuable Asset doesn't Appear on its Books

detail.title: The $20 Trillion Question: Why a Company's Most Valuable Asset doesn't Appear on its Books
detail.abstract:
Intangible assets now represent 90% of S&P 500 company value, with human capital comprising an estimated $20 trillion—roughly 55-60% of the $36 trillion gap between market and book values. Yet accounting standards treat all employee-related expenditures as expenses rather than investments, creating a fundamental disconnect between how value is created and how it is measured.

This misalignment distorts capital allocation decisions. When Meta laid off 21,000 workers in 2022-2023, its market value surged $40 billion because accounting treats workforce reductions as pure cost savings with no offsetting asset loss. Companies that invest heavily in training and development see profits depressed relative to competitors who churn through talent, even when the former strategy builds greater long-term value.

The paper examines why employees remain invisible on balance sheets despite executives universally declaring them the company's greatest asset. Sports leagues already capitalize contractual rights to player services where enforceable control exists. Acquisition accounting routinely records goodwill that substantially reflects assembled workforce capability. The inconsistency is stark: companies recognize human capital value when buying other firms but refuse to recognize the same value when built organically.

Several established valuation methodologies exist, including the Lev-Schwartz present value model, replacement cost approaches, contribution-based frameworks, and residual income methods. Each can be implemented through internal management reporting to improve decision quality around talent investment, retention, and development. The paper addresses substantive criticisms—commodification concerns, manipulation risk, and privacy issues—and proposes implementation designs using cohort-level valuations and regulatory safeguards.

Current accounting relies on imperfect models for depreciation, goodwill impairment, and inventory reserves. The relevant question is not whether human capital can be modeled perfectly, but whether trillion-dollar resource allocation decisions should continue while remaining blind to the asset that drives most modern value creation.

AI.tldr: 本文探讨了无形资产（特别是人力资本）在现代企业价值中的重要性，以及现行会计准则将其视为费用而非投资的问题。文章分析了人力资本在资产负债表上不可见的原因，并提出了多种估值方法来解决这一错配问题。
AI.research_question: 为什么员工作为公司最重要的资产，在资产负债表上却不可见？如何解决人力资本价值计量与价值创造之间的根本脱节？
AI.motivation: 无形资产占标普500公司价值的90%，人力资本估计达20万亿美元，占市值与账面价值之间36万亿美元差距的55-60%。但会计准则将所有员工相关支出视为费用而非投资，导致价值创造与计量方式之间的根本脱节。
AI.theoretical_framework: 人力资本理论、无形资产估值理论、会计计量理论、资源分配理论
AI.method: 理论分析、案例研究（如Meta裁员案例）、比较分析（体育联盟资本化球员合同与一般企业会计处理的对比）、现有估值方法评估（Lev-Schwartz现值模型、重置成本法、基于贡献的框架、剩余收益法）
AI.findings: 1. 会计准则将人力资本支出视为费用扭曲了资本分配决策；2. 公司收购时会确认反映人力资本价值的商誉，但拒绝承认内部构建的同等价值；3. 存在多种可行的人力资本估值方法；4. 可以通过内部管理报告改进人才投资决策
AI.theory_contributions: 1. 系统分析了人力资本在会计计量中的理论矛盾；2. 提出了解决人力资本价值可见性的理论框架；3. 拓展了无形资产会计理论的应用范围
AI.practical_contributions: 1. 为企业提供了改进人力资本投资决策的实用方法；2. 提出了解决商品化担忧、操纵风险和隐私问题的实施设计方案；3. 建议采用群体层面估值和监管保障措施

title: The Opposing Effects of Wealth on Younger and Older Entrepreneurs
affiliations: HEC Montreal - Department of Finance, Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia, University of Alberta - School of Business and University of Alberta - Department of Marketing, Business Economics & Law

detail.title: The Opposing Effects of Wealth on Younger and Older Entrepreneurs

publicationDetails.detailsText: FRB of Philadelphia Working Paper No. 25-32
publicationDetails.journalName: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: Using wealth windfalls from lottery winnings and matched employer-employee tax files, we compare the effect of additional wealth on the entrepreneurial activity of older and younger individuals. We find that additional wealth leads older winners (aged 55 to 64) to reduce business ownership and growth (as measured by sales, revenue, and employees). In contrast, extra wealth increases younger winners’ (aged 21 to 54) business ownership, but it has no effect on their business growth. The increase in business activity of a young winner does not offset the negative growth for an older winner, which may hurt economic growth.

AI.tldr: 通过分析彩票中奖者的财富意外增加对创业活动的影响，研究发现：55-64岁的中奖者会减少企业所有权和增长，而21-54岁的中奖者会增加企业所有权但企业增长无变化。
AI.research_question: 额外财富对不同年龄段个体创业活动的影响有何差异？
AI.motivation: 理解财富变化如何影响不同年龄段人群的创业决策，这对经济增长政策制定具有重要意义。
AI.theoretical_framework: 生命周期理论、创业动机理论、财富效应理论
AI.method: 利用彩票中奖作为财富外生冲击，结合雇主-雇员税收档案数据进行匹配分析
AI.findings: 1) 55-64岁中奖者：企业所有权和增长（销售额、收入、雇员数）下降；2) 21-54岁中奖者：企业所有权增加但企业增长无显著变化
AI.theory_contributions: 揭示了财富效应在创业决策中的年龄异质性，丰富了生命周期创业理论
AI.practical_contributions: 为针对不同年龄段的创业支持政策提供实证依据，提示需关注财富再分配对经济增长的潜在负面影响
